functions.name: SLIST_FIRST
functions.description: Returns the first element pointer of a singly-linked list head, or NULL if the list is empty.
requirements: head must be a pointer to an SLIST_HEAD(name, type) instance (or addressable object) that has been initialized (e.g., via SLIST_INIT or static initializer).
The head memory must be valid and readable.

functions.name: SLIST_END
functions.description: Macro that expands to NULL; used as the list end sentinel for singly-linked lists.
requirements: None beyond normal macro use; typically paired with SLIST_FIRST or comparisons.

functions.name: SLIST_EMPTY
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the singly-linked list is empty, zero otherwise.
requirements: head must be a pointer/reference to an initialized SLIST_HEAD.
head must be readable.

functions.name: SLIST_NEXT
functions.description: Returns the next element pointer following elm in a singly-linked list, or NULL if none.
requirements: elm must be a valid pointer to a list element whose structure includes the SLIST_ENTRY(type) named by field.
elm must be readable; field must be properly declared.

functions.name: SLIST_FOREACH
functions.signature: #define SLIST_FOREACH(var, head, field) for ((var) = SLIST_FIRST(head); (var) != SLIST_END(head); (var) = SLIST_NEXT(var, field))
functions.description: Iterates forward over all elements in a singly-linked list, assigning each element to var.
requirements: head must be an initialized SLIST_HEAD.
var must be a variable of pointer-to-element type compatible with the list element type.
The list must remain stable relative to iteration if you dereference var; modifying next pointers may break iteration unless carefully managed.

functions.name: SLIST_FOREACH_SAFE
functions.signature: #define SLIST_FOREACH_SAFE(var, head, field, tvar) for ((var) = SLIST_FIRST(head); (var) && ((tvar) = SLIST_NEXT(var, field), 1); (var) = (tvar))
functions.description: Iterates forward over a singly-linked list while allowing safe removal of the current element; tvar stores the next element.
requirements: head must be an initialized SLIST_HEAD.
var and tvar must be variables of pointer-to-element type.
If you remove var during the loop, use tvar for progression; do not invalidate tvar before the loop step.

functions.name: SLIST_INIT
functions.description: Initializes a singly-linked list head to the empty state.
requirements: head must be writable memory of an SLIST_HEAD instance.
Call before any other operations on this list head unless using SLIST_HEAD_INITIALIZER.

functions.name: SLIST_INSERT_AFTER
functions.description: Inserts elm immediately after slistelm in a singly-linked list.
requirements: slistelm must be an element currently linked in the target list.

functions.description: Removes and unlinks the element immediately following elm in a singly-linked list.

elm and the next element must be writable to update pointers.
field must match the SLIST_ENTRY in the element type.

functions.name: SLIST_REMOVE
functions.signature: #define SLIST_REMOVE(head, elm, type, field) do { if ((head)->slh_first == (elm)) { SLIST_REMOVE_HEAD((head), field); } else { struct type *curelm = (head)->slh_first; while (curelm->field.sle_next != (elm)) curelm = curelm->field.sle_next; curelm->field.sle_next = curelm->field.sle_next->field.sle_next; } _Q_INVALIDATE((elm)->field.sle_next); } while (0)
functions.description: Removes elm from a singly-linked list by searching for its predecessor when needed; invalidates elm->next in diagnostic builds.

type must be the element struct type used in the list; field must be the SLIST_ENTRY member name.
All involved pointers must be writable.
After removal, elm->field.sle_next must not be used (may be set to an invalid sentinel in debug/diagnostic builds).

field must be the XSIMPLEQ_ENTRY member in elm.

functions.name: XSIMPLEQ_INSERT_AFTER
functions.signature: #define XSIMPLEQ_INSERT_AFTER(head, listelm, elm, field) do { if (((elm)->field.sqx_next = (listelm)->field.sqx_next) == XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, NULL)) (head)->sqx_last = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, &(elm)->field.sqx_next); (listelm)->field.sqx_next = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, (elm)); } while (0)
functions.description: Inserts elm immediately after listelm in an XOR simple queue, updating the encoded last pointer if needed.
requirements: head must be the queue head for the list containing listelm and must be initialized.
listelm must currently be linked in the XOR simple queue.
elm must not be already linked in an XSIMPLEQ.
All involved memory must be writable; field must be the XSIMPLEQ_ENTRY member.

functions.name: XSIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD
functions.signature: #define XSIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD(head, field) do { if (((head)->sqx_first = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, (head)->sqx_first)->field.sqx_next) == XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, NULL)) (head)->sqx_last = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, &(head)->sqx_first); } while (0)
functions.description: Removes the head element from an XOR simple queue, updating the encoded last pointer if the queue becomes empty.
requirements: head must be an initialized XSIMPLEQ_HEAD whose first element is not encoded NULL.
head and the first element must be writable.
field must be the XSIMPLEQ_ENTRY member.

functions.name: XSIMPLEQ_REMOVE_AFTER
functions.signature: #define XSIMPLEQ_REMOVE_AFTER(head, elm, field) do { if (((elm)->field.sqx_next = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, (elm)->field.sqx_next)->field.sqx_next) == XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, NULL)) (head)->sqx_last = XSIMPLEQ_XOR(head, &(elm)->field.sqx_next); } while (0)
functions.description: Removes the element immediately following elm in an XOR simple queue, updating the encoded last pointer if the removed element was the last.
requirements: head must be an initialized XSIMPLEQ_HEAD.
elm must be linked in the queue and have a non-NULL decoded next element.
All involved memory must be writable; field must be the XSIMPLEQ_ENTRY member.

functions.name: TAILQ_FIRST
functions.description: Returns the first element pointer of a tail queue, or NULL if empty.
requirements: head must be a pointer/reference to an initialized TAILQ_HEAD and readable.

functions.name: TAILQ_END
functions.description: Macro that expands to NULL; used as the end sentinel for a tail queue.
requirements: None.

functions.name: TAILQ_NEXT
functions.description: Returns the next element pointer in a tail queue, or NULL if none.
requirements: elm must be a valid pointer to a tail queue element having TAILQ_ENTRY named by field.
elm must be readable.

functions.name: TAILQ_LAST
functions.description: Returns the last element pointer in a tail queue by dereferencing the tail pointer stored in the head, or NULL if empty.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD of type 'struct headname'.
headname must be the exact tag name used in the TAILQ_HEAD declaration for this head.
head must be readable; stored pointers must be valid.

functions.name: TAILQ_PREV
functions.description: Returns the previous element pointer in a tail queue by dereferencing the stored back-pointer in elm.
requirements: elm must be a valid pointer to an element linked into a tail queue declared with head tag 'struct headname'.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member in the element struct.
elm and the stored back-pointer must be readable; invariants must hold (i.e., elm is linked).

functions.name: TAILQ_EMPTY
functions.description: Returns nonzero if a tail queue is empty, zero otherwise.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD and readable.

functions.name: TAILQ_FOREACH
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_FOREACH(var, head, field) for ((var) = TAILQ_FIRST(head); (var) != TAILQ_END(head); (var) = TAILQ_NEXT(var, field))
functions.description: Iterates forward over all elements in a tail queue.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD.
var must be of pointer-to-element type compatible with the queue element type.

functions.name: TAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE(var, head, field, tvar) for ((var) = TAILQ_FIRST(head); (var) != TAILQ_END(head) && ((tvar) = TAILQ_NEXT(var, field), 1); (var) = (tvar))
functions.description: Iterates forward over a tail queue while allowing safe removal of var; tvar stores the next element.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD.
var and tvar must be variables of pointer-to-element type compatible with the tail queue.

functions.name: TAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE(var, head, headname, field) for ((var) = TAILQ_LAST(head, headname); (var) != TAILQ_END(head); (var) = TAILQ_PREV(var, headname, field))
functions.description: Iterates backward over all elements in a tail queue, from last to first.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD of type 'struct headname'.
var must be a pointer-to-element variable; field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member in the element type.
headname must match the TAILQ_HEAD declaration.

functions.name: TAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE_SAFE
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE_SAFE(var, head, headname, field, tvar) for ((var) = TAILQ_LAST(head, headname); (var) != TAILQ_END(head) && ((tvar) = TAILQ_PREV(var, headname, field), 1); (var) = (tvar))
functions.description: Iterates backward over a tail queue while allowing safe removal of the current element; tvar stores the previous element.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD of type 'struct headname'.
var and tvar must be variables of pointer-to-element type compatible with the element type.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member; headname must match the TAILQ_HEAD declaration.

functions.name: TAILQ_INIT
functions.description: Initializes a tail queue head to the empty state.
requirements: head must be writable memory representing a TAILQ_HEAD.

functions.name: TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD(head, elm, field) do { if (((elm)->field.tqe_next = (head)->tqh_first) != NULL) (head)->tqh_first->field.tqe_prev = &(elm)->field.tqe_next; else (head)->tqh_last = &(elm)->field.tqe_next; (head)->tqh_first = (elm); (elm)->field.tqe_prev = &(head)->tqh_first; } while (0)
functions.description: Inserts elm at the head of a tail queue, updating both head and tail as needed.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD and writable.
elm must not be currently linked in any tail queue; its linkage will be overwritten.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member in elm.

functions.name: TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL(head, elm, field) do { (elm)->field.tqe_next = NULL; (elm)->field.tqe_prev = (head)->tqh_last; *(head)->tqh_last = (elm); (head)->tqh_last = &(elm)->field.tqe_next; } while (0)
functions.description: Inserts elm at the tail of a tail queue.
requirements: head must be an initialized TAILQ_HEAD and writable.
elm must not be currently linked in any tail queue; its linkage will be initialized.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member in elm.

functions.name: TAILQ_INSERT_AFTER
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_INSERT_AFTER(head, listelm, elm, field) do { if (((elm)->field.tqe_next = (listelm)->field.tqe_next) != NULL) (elm)->field.tqe_next->field.tqe_prev = &(elm)->field.tqe_next; else (head)->tqh_last = &(elm)->field.tqe_next; (listelm)->field.tqe_next = (elm); (elm)->field.tqe_prev = &(listelm)->field.tqe_next; } while (0)
functions.description: Inserts elm immediately after listelm in a tail queue, updating tail if needed.
requirements: head must be the TAILQ_HEAD for the queue containing listelm and must be initialized.
listelm must be currently linked in the queue.
elm must not be currently linked in any tail queue; its linkage will be set.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member.

functions.name: TAILQ_INSERT_BEFORE
functions.description: Inserts elm immediately before listelm in a tail queue.
requirements: listelm must be currently linked in a tail queue.
elm must not be currently linked in any tail queue; its linkage will be initialized.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member.

functions.name: TAILQ_REMOVE
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_REMOVE(head, elm, field) do { if (((elm)->field.tqe_next) != NULL) (elm)->field.tqe_next->field.tqe_prev = (elm)->field.tqe_prev; else (head)->tqh_last = (elm)->field.tqe_prev; *(elm)->field.tqe_prev = (elm)->field.tqe_next; _Q_INVALIDATE((elm)->field.tqe_prev); _Q_INVALIDATE((elm)->field.tqe_next); } while (0)
functions.description: Removes elm from a tail queue, relinking neighbors and updating tail if needed; invalidates elm's linkage in debug/diagnostic builds.
requirements: head must be the TAILQ_HEAD for the queue and initialized.
elm must be currently linked in the queue (tqe_prev must point to predecessor's next or head pointer).
All involved memory must be writable.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member in the element type.
After removal, do not use elm->field.tqe_prev/tqe_next (may be invalidated).

functions.name: TAILQ_REPLACE
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_REPLACE(head, elm, elm2, field) do { if (((elm2)->field.tqe_next = (elm)->field.tqe_next) != NULL) (elm2)->field.tqe_next->field.tqe_prev = &(elm2)->field.tqe_next; else (head)->tqh_last = &(elm2)->field.tqe_next; (elm2)->field.tqe_prev = (elm)->field.tqe_prev; *(elm2)->field.tqe_prev = (elm2); _Q_INVALIDATE((elm)->field.tqe_prev); _Q_INVALIDATE((elm)->field.tqe_next); } while (0)
functions.description: Replaces elm in a tail queue with elm2, preserving position and neighbors; invalidates elm's linkage in debug/diagnostic builds.
requirements: head must be the TAILQ_HEAD for the queue and initialized.
elm must be currently linked in the queue.
elm2 must not be currently linked; its linkage will be initialized.
field must be the TAILQ_ENTRY member.
All involved memory must be writable; after replacement, do not use elm's linkage fields.

functions.name: TAILQ_CONCAT
functions.signature: #define TAILQ_CONCAT(head1, head2, field) do { if (!TAILQ_EMPTY(head2)) { *(head1)->tqh_last = (head2)->tqh_first; (head2)->tqh_first->field.tqe_prev = (head1)->tqh_last; (head1)->tqh_last = (head2)->tqh_last; TAILQ_INIT((head2)); } } while (0)
functions.description: Appends all elements from head2 to the tail of head1, fixes back-pointers, and reinitializes head2 to empty.
requirements: head1 and head2 must be initialized TAILQ_HEADs of the same element type and writable.
After concatenation, head2 is reset to empty; do not rely on its old first/last pointers.

functions.name: ssh_err
functions.description: Translate a numeric ssh error code to a human-readable error string. Typical usage: pass one of the SSH_ERR_* constants defined in this header and receive a descriptive message suitable for logs or diagnostics. The returned pointer refers to a constant, read-only string; ownership is not transferred. Specific contents and completeness of messages for unrecognized codes are not documented here.
requirements: Argument n should be an SSH error code defined in this header (e.g., SSH_ERR_SUCCESS, SSH_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR, etc.).
The returned const char* points to read-only storage; the caller must not modify or free it.
Behavior for values of n not corresponding to a defined SSH_ERR_* constant is unspecified in this header (may return a generic/unknown message).
No error reporting via errno or exceptions is documented; callers should rely solely on the returned string.

functions.name: sshbuf_new_label
functions.description: Allocates a new sshbuf and assigns it a label (typically for debugging/traceability). Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Label pointer may be NULL or a C string; maximum label length is constrained by MAX_LABEL_LEN (64) in this header.
Caller must check for NULL return before use.
Caller owns the returned buffer and must free it with sshbuf_free.

functions.name: sshbuf_relabel
functions.description: Updates the human-readable label of an existing sshbuf. Intended for diagnostics/identification.
requirements: The sshbuf pointer must be a valid, initialized buffer.
Label pointer may be NULL or a C string; effective maximum enforced by implementation (MAX_LABEL_LEN is defined).
Does not transfer ownership; buffer remains valid.

functions.name: sshbuf_type
functions.description: Assigns a type tag (from enum buffer_types) to a buffer to identify its purpose.
requirements: sshbuf must be a valid, initialized buffer.
Type must be a value from enum buffer_types.

functions.name: sshbuf_from
functions.description: Creates a new, read-only sshbuf that references existing data blob of specified length.
requirements: blob must point to at least len bytes of stable memory that will not change for the lifetime of the sshbuf.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check.
Caller must free the returned sshbuf with sshbuf_free when done.

functions.name: sshbuf_fromb
functions.description: Creates a new, read-only sshbuf referencing the contents of another buffer. Source content must not change during lifetime of the new buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
Underlying contents of buf must remain unchanged for the lifetime of the returned buffer.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check.
Caller must free the returned sshbuf with sshbuf_free.

functions.name: sshbuf_froms
functions.description: Consumes an SSH wire-encoded string from buf and produces a new, read-only sshbuf that references the string’s contents without copying. Places the new buffer in *bufp.
requirements: buf must contain an SSH string (u32 length followed by that many bytes).
buf must be valid and readable; on success the consumed string is removed from buf.
bufp must be non-NULL and writable; on success *bufp receives a newly allocated sshbuf the caller must free via sshbuf_free.
Returns 0 on success or a negative SSH_ERR_* code on failure; caller must check and handle errors.

functions.name: sshbuf_free
functions.description: Clears and frees a buffer and any associated resources.
requirements: buf may be NULL (safe to call) or a valid sshbuf.
After return, buf pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: sshbuf_reset
functions.description: Resets a buffer to empty, preserving its maximum size. Does not free memory.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
All previously reserved pointers into the buffer become invalid after reset.

functions.name: sshbuf_max_size
functions.description: Returns the configured maximum usable size for the buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.

functions.name: sshbuf_set_max_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum usable size of the buffer. Buffer may temporarily use up to ~2x this memory plus overhead.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
max_size must be within implementation limits (<= SSHBUF_SIZE_MAX).
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure; caller must handle errors.

functions.name: sshbuf_len
functions.description: Returns the number of data bytes currently stored in the buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.

functions.name: sshbuf_avail
functions.description: Returns the number of additional bytes that can be appended before hitting max_size.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.

functions.name: sshbuf_ptr
functions.description: Returns a read-only pointer to the start of the buffer’s data.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf with any length (may be zero).
Returned pointer becomes invalid after any modifying sshbuf call.

functions.name: sshbuf_mutable_ptr
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the start of the buffer’s data, or NULL if the buffer is read-only.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
Do not use if the buffer is read-only (function returns NULL).
Pointer becomes invalid after any modifying sshbuf call.

functions.name: sshbuf_check_reserve
functions.signature: int sshbuf_check_reserve(const struct sshbuf *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Checks whether reserving len additional bytes would succeed, handling overflow safely. Does not modify the buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
Returns 0 if reservation would succeed or negative SSH_ERR_* otherwise; caller must handle errors before attempting to reserve.

functions.name: sshbuf_allocate
functions.description: Preallocates len additional bytes to minimize future reallocations. Does not increase logical length.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf.
len must not exceed available capacity constraints (max_size and limits).
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure; caller must handle errors.

functions.name: sshbuf_reserve
functions.signature: int sshbuf_reserve(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t len, u_char **dpp);
functions.description: Reserves len bytes at the end of the buffer and optionally returns a pointer to the first reserved byte via dpp for direct writing.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf and not read-only.
len must be > 0 and within available capacity.
If dpp is non-NULL, it must be writable to receive the pointer; the memory remains valid until the next modifying call.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure; caller must handle errors.

functions.name: sshbuf_consume
functions.description: Consumes (removes) len bytes from the start of the buffer, advancing the read position.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf and contain at least len data bytes.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_consume_end
functions.description: Consumes (removes) len bytes from the end of the buffer, shrinking its length.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf and contain at least len data bytes.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get
functions.signature: int sshbuf_get(struct sshbuf *buf, void *v, size_t len);
functions.description: Extracts len bytes from the start of buf into v and consumes them.
requirements: buf must be a valid sshbuf and contain at least len bytes.
v must point to a writable memory region of size >= len.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put
functions.signature: int sshbuf_put(struct sshbuf *buf, const void *v, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends len bytes from v to the end of buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with sufficient available space or expandable within limits.
v must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_putb
functions.signature: int sshbuf_putb(struct sshbuf *buf, const struct sshbuf *v);
functions.description: Appends all data from buffer v to buffer buf.
requirements: Both buf and v must be valid sshbufs; buf must be writable.
Sufficient capacity must be available or expandable within limits.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_putf
functions.description: Formats text using printf-style fmt and arguments and appends the result to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string with matching arguments.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_putfv
functions.signature: int sshbuf_putfv(struct sshbuf *buf, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of sshbuf_putf that appends formatted data to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; ap must be initialized.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_u64
functions.description: Extracts a big-endian 64-bit unsigned integer from the start of buf and consumes it.
requirements: buf must contain at least 8 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL to receive the value.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_u32
functions.description: Extracts a big-endian 32-bit unsigned integer from buf and consumes it.
requirements: buf must contain at least 4 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_u16
functions.description: Extracts a big-endian 16-bit unsigned integer from buf and consumes it.
requirements: buf must contain at least 2 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_u8
functions.description: Extracts an 8-bit unsigned value from buf and consumes it.
requirements: buf must contain at least 1 byte.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_u64
functions.description: Appends a big-endian 64-bit unsigned integer to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_u32
functions.description: Appends a big-endian 32-bit unsigned integer to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_u16
functions.description: Appends a big-endian 16-bit unsigned integer to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_u8
functions.description: Appends an 8-bit unsigned value to buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_peek_u64
functions.signature: int sshbuf_peek_u64(const struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int64_t *valp);
functions.description: Reads a big-endian 64-bit value at offset without modifying the buffer.
requirements: buf must contain at least offset+8 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_peek_u32
functions.signature: int sshbuf_peek_u32(const struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int32_t *valp);
functions.description: Reads a big-endian 32-bit value at offset without modifying the buffer.
requirements: buf must contain at least offset+4 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_peek_u16
functions.signature: int sshbuf_peek_u16(const struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int16_t *valp);
functions.description: Reads a big-endian 16-bit value at offset without modifying the buffer.
requirements: buf must contain at least offset+2 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_peek_u8
functions.signature: int sshbuf_peek_u8(const struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_char *valp);
functions.description: Reads an 8-bit value at offset without modifying the buffer.
requirements: buf must contain at least offset+1 bytes.
valp must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_poke_u64
functions.signature: int sshbuf_poke_u64(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int64_t val);
functions.description: Overwrites 8 bytes at offset with big-endian 64-bit val. Destination bytes must already exist.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf.
Buffer must contain at least offset+8 bytes; no resize occurs.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_poke_u32
functions.signature: int sshbuf_poke_u32(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int32_t val);
functions.description: Overwrites 4 bytes at offset with big-endian 32-bit val. Destination must exist.
requirements: buf must be valid and writable with at least offset+4 bytes present.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_poke_u16
functions.signature: int sshbuf_poke_u16(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_int16_t val);
functions.description: Overwrites 2 bytes at offset with big-endian 16-bit val. Destination must exist.
requirements: buf must be valid and writable with at least offset+2 bytes present.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_poke_u8
functions.signature: int sshbuf_poke_u8(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, u_char val);
functions.description: Overwrites 1 byte at offset with val. Destination must exist.
requirements: buf must be valid and writable with at least offset+1 bytes present.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_poke
functions.signature: int sshbuf_poke(struct sshbuf *buf, size_t offset, void *v, size_t len);
functions.description: Overwrites len bytes at offset with the bytes from v. Destination bytes must already exist.
requirements: buf must be valid and writable.
Buffer must contain at least offset+len bytes; no resize occurs.
v must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_string
functions.description: Extracts an SSH wire-encoded string (u32 length followed by data) from buf, consuming it, and returns a newly allocated copy in *valp and its length in *lenp.
requirements: buf must contain a complete SSH string.
valp must be non-NULL; caller must free *valp on success.
lenp may be NULL; if non-NULL it receives the length.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_cstring
functions.description: Extracts an SSH string from buf that must not contain NUL bytes, returning a newly allocated C string in *valp and its length in *lenp. Consumes the string from buf.
requirements: buf must contain a complete SSH string with no embedded NULs.
valp must be non-NULL; caller must free *valp on success.
lenp may be NULL; if non-NULL it receives the length.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_stringb
functions.description: Extracts an SSH string from buf and appends its contents into buffer v. Consumes the string from buf.
requirements: buf must contain a complete SSH string.
v must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_string
functions.signature: int sshbuf_put_string(struct sshbuf *buf, const void *v, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends an SSH wire-encoded string to buf (u32 length then len bytes from v).
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable sshbuf with capacity.
v must point to at least len bytes; len may be zero.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_cstring
functions.description: Appends an SSH wire-encoded string that represents a C string v (no embedded NULs expected).
requirements: buf must be valid and writable with capacity.
v must be a valid C string; behavior on embedded NULs is not accepted by cstring semantics.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_put_stringb
functions.signature: int sshbuf_put_stringb(struct sshbuf *buf, const struct sshbuf *v);
functions.description: Appends an SSH wire-encoded string to buf from the contents of buffer v (length prefix plus v’s data).
requirements: buf must be valid and writable with capacity.
v must be a valid sshbuf (readable).
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_get_string_direct
functions.signature: int sshbuf_get_string_direct(struct sshbuf *buf, const u_char **valp, size_t *lenp);
functions.description: Directly returns a pointer into buf for the next SSH string without copying, consuming it. Pointer remains valid until the next modifying call.
requirements: buf must contain a complete SSH string.
valp may be NULL; if non-NULL it receives a pointer valid until next modification.
lenp may be NULL; if non-NULL it receives the length.
Returns 0 on success or negative SSH_ERR_* on failure.

functions.name: sshbuf_peek_string_direct

requirements: First argument must be a valid RSA hash/alg ID.

Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure (inferred).

functions.signature: int ssh_ed25519_encode_store_sig(const u_char *, size_t, u_char **, size_t *);
functions.description: Encode an Ed25519 signature into SSH wire-format and return it as a newly allocated buffer and length.

Output pointers must be non-NULL; caller frees *out on success.
Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure (inferred).

functions.signature: int ssh_rsa_complete_crt_parameters(const BIGNUM *, const BIGNUM *, const BIGNUM *, const BIGNUM *, BIGNUM **, BIGNUM **);
functions.description: Compute and output missing RSA CRT parameters (dp, dq, or qinv) from the provided primes/exponents. Marked as used by ssh-keygen.

functions.name: cipher_by_name
functions.description: Looks up a cipher algorithm descriptor by its name. Returns a pointer to an sshcipher definition matching the provided name or NULL if not found. Typically used before initializing a cipher context.
requirements: The name pointer must be non-NULL and point to a NUL-terminated string.
The name should match a supported cipher algorithm identifier; otherwise the function may return NULL.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.

functions.name: cipher_warning_message
functions.description: Returns a human-readable warning or informational message associated with a cipher context, or NULL/empty when no warning applies. Useful to surface deprecation notices or configuration caveats.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized struct sshcipher_ctx pointer (non-NULL).
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by the library and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: ciphers_valid
functions.description: Validates a comma-separated (or similar) list of cipher names. Returns non-zero if the list is acceptable/supported, zero otherwise.
requirements: The input string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
Cipher names should use the expected format (implementation-defined); invalid or unknown names will cause a failure.
Caller should check the integer return value to determine validity.

functions.name: cipher_alg_list
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated string listing supported cipher algorithms, formatted according to the given separator and flags. Typically used for configuration display or negotiation.
requirements: The separator character determines how algorithms are delimited (e.g., ',').
The int flag likely controls filtering (e.g., multithread support vs. all); exact semantics are implementation-defined.
The returned string is heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller using the appropriate deallocator (e.g., free).

functions.name: compression_alg_list
functions.description: Returns a string listing supported compression algorithms, possibly filtered or formatted based on the input flag. The returned memory is library-owned.
requirements: Flag meaning is implementation-defined; pass 0 for defaults unless otherwise documented.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller and remains valid per library lifetime guarantees.

functions.name: cipher_init
functions.signature: int cipher_init(struct sshcipher_ctx **, const struct sshcipher *, const u_char *, u_int, const u_char *, u_int, u_int, int, int);
functions.description: Initializes (or allocates and initializes) a cipher context for encryption or decryption using the specified cipher, key, and IV. Additional parameters select direction and possibly threading behavior. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: The output context pointer (struct sshcipher_ctx **) must be non-NULL; on success, it will reference an initialized context that must later be freed with cipher_free.
The cipher descriptor pointer must be a valid struct sshcipher obtained from cipher_by_name or equivalent and non-NULL.
The key pointer must reference at least keylen bytes as required by the selected cipher; the provided u_int key length must match the actual available bytes.

The IV pointer, if required by the cipher, must reference at least ivlen bytes as required by the selected cipher; the provided u_int IV length must match the actual available bytes. For ciphers that do not use an IV, pass length 0 and a NULL or ignored pointer as appropriate.
The u_int parameter preceding the two ints is likely a sequence number or reserved; pass 0 unless otherwise documented.
The int parameters select mode/direction and threading (e.g., CIPHER_ENCRYPT/CIPHER_DECRYPT and CIPHER_MULTITHREAD/CIPHER_SERIAL); use the defined macros from this header.
Caller must check the return value; non-zero indicates initialization failure and the output context must not be used.

functions.name: cipher_crypt
functions.signature: int cipher_crypt(struct sshcipher_ctx *, u_int, u_char *, const u_char *, u_int, u_int, u_int);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using an initialized cipher context. Processes input from src into dst according to context direction and parameters, and may use sequence/aad lengths as indicated by the u_int parameters. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, successfully initialized cipher context (non-NULL).
dst must point to a buffer with capacity for at least the number of output bytes to be written; typically at least 'len' bytes (implementation-defined).
src must point to at least 'len' readable bytes; it may be the same as dst only if the implementation supports in-place operation (unknown from this header).
The u_int parameters represent lengths/counters (e.g., sequence number, input length, AAD length). Use values consistent with the algorithm and with any earlier calls; avoid overflow of u_int.
Caller must check the return value; non-zero indicates an error and output should not be used.

functions.name: cipher_get_length
functions.signature: int cipher_get_length(struct sshcipher_ctx *, u_int *, u_int, const u_char *, u_int);
functions.description: Derives or validates the plaintext packet length from an encrypted packet prefix and context state (commonly for length fields protected by the cipher). Writes the resulting length to the provided output pointer. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized cipher context (non-NULL).
lenp must be a non-NULL pointer to u_int for receiving the computed length.
The const u_char * buffer must contain at least 'buflen' readable bytes; 'buflen' must be sufficient for the algorithm’s length extraction (implementation-defined minimum).
The u_int parameter preceding the buffer is typically a sequence number or similar and must match the stream position expected by ctx.
Caller must check the return value before using *lenp.

functions.name: cipher_free
functions.description: Releases and wipes a cipher context created by cipher_init, freeing associated resources. Safe to call on contexts that are no longer needed.
requirements: If ctx is non-NULL, it must have been initialized by cipher_init (or compatible) and not already freed.
After this call, ctx is invalid and must not be used again.

functions.name: cipher_blocksize
functions.description: Returns the cipher’s block size in bytes (or 1 for stream ciphers).
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Caller should not assume non-zero; for stream ciphers this may return 1.

functions.name: cipher_rekey_blocks
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of blocks that may be processed before rekeying is required for the given cipher. Used to enforce cryptographic safety limits.
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Caller must treat 0 as unknown/unspecified and handle rekeying policy accordingly (semantics implementation-defined).

functions.name: cipher_keylen
functions.description: Returns the required key length in bytes for the specified cipher.
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Use the returned length to size key buffers passed to cipher_init.

functions.name: cipher_seclen
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of secret material for the cipher (may include key, IV seed, or related secret length as defined by the implementation).
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Interpretation of this length is implementation-defined; use alongside cipher_keylen/ivlen as documented by the implementation.

functions.name: cipher_authlen
functions.description: Returns the authentication tag length in bytes for AEAD ciphers, or 0 for ciphers without authentication.
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Callers using AEAD modes must provision space for the tag as indicated by this value.

functions.name: cipher_ivlen
functions.description: Returns the initialization vector (IV) length in bytes required by the cipher (0 for ciphers that do not use an IV).
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Use this length to size IV buffers for cipher_init and get/set IV operations.

functions.name: cipher_is_cbc
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the cipher uses CBC mode; returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: The cipher descriptor pointer must be non-NULL and reference a valid sshcipher.
Do not rely on exact return value beyond zero/non-zero semantics.

functions.name: cipher_reset_multithreaded
functions.description: Resets internal multithreading state/selection for cipher operations. Intended for reinitializing thread-related resources or switching behavior.
requirements: May affect global/shared state; callers should ensure no concurrent cipher operations are in progress when calling this function.
Call order and side effects are implementation-defined.

functions.name: cipher_ctx_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the cipher algorithm associated with the given context as a NUL-terminated string.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized cipher context (non-NULL).
The returned pointer is library-owned and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: cipher_ctx_is_plaintext
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the provided context represents a plaintext/no-encryption configuration, zero otherwise. Useful to short-circuit encryption paths.
requirements: ctx must be a valid cipher context pointer (non-NULL).
Caller should treat any non-zero as true; exact values are not specified.

functions.name: cipher_get_keyiv
functions.description: Retrieves the current IV (or nonce) from a cipher context into the provided buffer. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized cipher context (non-NULL).
buf must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least 'len' bytes.
'len' should be at least the IV length for the cipher (see cipher_ivlen for the cipher associated with the context).
Caller must check the return value before using the buffer contents.

functions.name: cipher_set_keyiv
functions.signature: int cipher_set_keyiv(struct sshcipher_ctx *, const u_char *, size_t);
functions.description: Sets or updates the IV (or nonce) of the cipher context from the provided buffer. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized cipher context (non-NULL).
buf must be non-NULL and reference at least 'len' readable bytes containing the IV.
'len' must match the IV length required by the context's cipher (see cipher_ivlen for the cipher associated with the context).
Caller must check the return value; on failure the context's IV may remain unchanged.

functions.name: ssh_init
functions.signature: int ssh_init(struct ssh **, int is_server, struct kex_params *kex_params);
functions.description: Create and initialize an SSH connection object with optional key exchange parameters. Expected usage: call once to obtain a connection handle before any packet processing or key exchange. Notes: the first parameter is an output pointer receiving the newly created struct ssh*; is_server selects server vs client mode; kex_params (optional) may provide initial key-exchange proposals.
requirements: The first argument must point to storage for a struct ssh* that will receive the created handle.
If kex_params is non-NULL, its contents (proposal array) must be properly initialized for use.
Must be called before using the returned struct ssh* with any other SSH API functions.
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_free
functions.description: Release all state associated with an SSH connection created by ssh_init. Expected usage: call when finished with the SSH connection to free resources. Notes: the handle must not be used after this call.
requirements: The ssh argument must be a valid connection previously created by ssh_init.
Do not use the ssh pointer after this function returns (it becomes invalid).
Must not be called on a NULL or already-freed handle (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: ssh_set_app_data
functions.description: Attach application-specific data to the SSH connection state. Expected usage: store a user-defined context pointer for later retrieval via ssh_get_app_data.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
The data pointer may be NULL or any application-managed pointer; lifetime management is the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: ssh_get_app_data
functions.description: Retrieve the application-specific data pointer previously set on the SSH connection via ssh_set_app_data. Returns the stored pointer or possibly NULL if none was set.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.

functions.name: ssh_add_hostkey
functions.description: Register a private or public host key with the SSH connection. Expected usage: call before initiating key exchange so the library can use the key (server) or verify the server’s host key (client). Notes: private host keys are needed for server mode; public host keys are used to verify the server in client mode.
requirements: Must be called before a key exchange is initiated with ssh_packet_next().
The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
The key argument must be a valid struct sshkey (private key required to act as a server; public key used to verify the server’s host key).
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_set_verify_host_key_callback
functions.signature: int ssh_set_verify_host_key_callback(struct ssh *ssh, int (*cb)(struct sshkey *, struct ssh *));
functions.description: Register a custom host-key verification callback to override the default verification. Expected usage: set a callback that returns 0 if the host key is acceptable and -1 if verification fails. Notes: install this before verification occurs during key exchange/handshake.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
The cb function must match signature int (struct sshkey *, struct ssh *).
The cb must return 0 for success and -1 to indicate verification failure.
Should be set before any host-key verification is needed (typically before or during key exchange).
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_packet_next
functions.description: Advance to the next input packet, performing decryption and handling key exchange internally. On progress, writes the packet type to typep. If no new packet is available, it sets typep and the caller must feed more input via ssh_input_append and send pending output (from ssh_output_ptr) to allow key exchange to proceed.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
typep must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the packet type.

When no packet is available, the caller must append received network data to the input stream via ssh_input_append() and send any pending output obtained via ssh_output_ptr(); after sending, consume it with ssh_output_consume().
Do not assume the function blocks; it operates over the maintained input/output byte-streams.
Error handling: the return value indicates status/success (exact semantics are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_packet_payload
functions.description: Return a pointer to the raw payload of the current input packet and its length. The returned buffer is valid only until the next call to ssh_packet_next.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection with a current packet available.
lenp must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the payload length.
The returned payload pointer becomes invalid after the next ssh_packet_next() call; do not access it thereafter.

functions.name: ssh_packet_put
functions.signature: int ssh_packet_put(struct ssh *ssh, int type, const u_char *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Create an encrypted packet with the given type and payload and append it to the connection’s output byte-stream. Expected usage: queue packets for transmission, then obtain and send bytes via ssh_output_ptr/ssh_output_consume.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (may be NULL if len is 0).
type must be a valid SSH packet type (exact range unspecified here).
After queuing, the caller is responsible for sending the resulting output stream over the network via ssh_output_ptr() and then calling ssh_output_consume() to remove sent bytes.
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_input_space
functions.description: Check whether len bytes can be appended to the input byte-stream. Expected usage: optionally probe capacity before calling ssh_input_append.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
len specifies the number of bytes the caller intends to append.
Error handling: the return value indicates whether space is available (exact semantics/codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_input_append
functions.signature: int ssh_input_append(struct ssh *ssh, const u_char *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Append data to the connection’s input byte-stream. Expected usage: feed bytes received from the network so ssh_packet_next can process them.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (may be NULL if len is 0).
Caller should ensure enough input space is available (e.g., via ssh_input_space) before appending, if necessary.
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_output_space
functions.description: Check whether len bytes can be appended to the output byte-stream. Note: marked with XXX in the header; details may be subject to change or not fully defined here.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
len specifies the number of bytes the caller intends to append to the output stream.
Error handling: the return value indicates whether space is available (exact semantics/codes are not specified here).

functions.name: ssh_output_ptr
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer and length for the current output byte-stream to send over the network. After successfully sending some or all bytes, call ssh_output_consume to remove the sent bytes from the stream.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes available to send.
The caller must transmit the returned bytes over the network and then call ssh_output_consume() with the number of bytes actually sent.
The returned pointer may become invalid after consumption or further output modifications; use it promptly.

functions.name: ssh_output_consume
functions.description: Remove len bytes from the beginning of the output byte-stream after they have been successfully sent over the network.
requirements: The ssh argument must reference a valid SSH connection.
len must be less than or equal to the number of bytes currently available in the output stream (exact error behavior unspecified).
Should be called only after those bytes have been transmitted to the peer.
Error handling: the return value indicates success/failure (exact codes are not specified here).

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid and interesting byte strings for sshbuf-related fuzzers.
# It focuses on SSH wire string patterns, C-strings without NULs, printable labels, and
# mixtures thereof, because the target stubs frequently pass FUZZ_PARAM_STR into:
#  - sshbuf_new_label (label <= 64)
#  - sshbuf_from (arbitrary bytes, up to 1024)
#  - sshbuf_put/put_string/get_string/get_cstring/... (payloads up to 256/512)
# It returns a single bytes buffer that the harness will use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and similar calls. We bias toward valid SSH wire-encoded strings and printable labels
# to maximize code coverage, but still include a variety of sizes and character classes.

PRINTABLE = bytes([c for c in range(0x20, 0x7f)])

def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choices(PRINTABLE, k=n))

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return r.randbytes(n) if hasattr(r, 'randbytes') else bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _ssh_wire_string(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # SSH wire string: 4-byte big-endian length + payload
    return struct.pack('>I', len(payload)) + payload

def _make_label(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Labels used by sshbuf_new_label: limit 64, typically printable, may include colon, dash.
    # Produce a variety of lengths with bias toward small but non-empty.
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    pick = r.choice(choices)
    if pick == 0:
        n = r.randint(1, 8)
    elif pick == 1:
        n = r.randint(9, 32)
    elif pick == 2:
        n = r.randint(33, 64)
    elif pick == 3:
        # Edge: exactly 64
        n = 64
    else:
        # Include a few with embedded spaces and punctuation
        n = r.randint(5, 48)
    base = _rand_printable(r, n)
    # Mix in characters often used in labels
    extras = b"-_:,./@"
    barray = bytearray(base)
    for i in range(0, len(barray), max(1, len(barray)//(1 + r.randint(1, 6)))):
        barray[i] = r.choice(extras)
    return bytes(barray)

def _make_cstring_payload(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # For sshbuf_get_cstring: no embedded NULs. Use printable set.
    n = r.randint(0, max_len)
    return _rand_printable(r, n)

def _make_arbitrary_payload(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Arbitrary bytes, can include NULs
    n = r.randint(0, max_len)
    return _rand_bytes(r, n)

def _make_repeated_pattern(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    token = _rand_printable(r, r.randint(1, min(16, max_len or 1)))
    reps = 0 if max_len == 0 else r.randint(0, max(1, max_len // max(1, len(token))))
    s = (token * reps)[:max_len]
    return s

def _make_mixed_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a blob combining several useful forms to feed multiple consumers sequentially.
    # Layout:
    #  - Label (<=64), NUL-terminated (safe for %s)
    #  - SSH wire string with arbitrary bytes (len <= 512)
    #  - SSH wire string with cstring (no NULs) (len <= 256)
    #  - Plain payload chunk for sshbuf_put/putf (<= 256)
    #  - Another label for relabel
    label1 = _make_label(r)
    cstr_label1 = label1.replace(b"\x00", b"-")
    part_label1 = cstr_label1[:64]

    arb_payload = _make_arbitrary_payload(r, 512)
    wire1 = _ssh_wire_string(arb_payload)

    cstr_payload = _make_cstring_payload(r, 256)
    wire2 = _ssh_wire_string(cstr_payload)

    plain = _make_arbitrary_payload(r, 256)

    label2 = _make_label(r)[:64]

    # Optionally include a small printable piece for ssh_packet_* printf formats
    fmt_piece = _make_cstring_payload(r, 64)

    # Combine with small separators that are harmless if treated as opaque bytes
    sep = b"\n"
    blob = sep.join([part_label1, wire1, wire2, plain, label2, fmt_piece])
    return blob

def _ensure_size_limit(b: bytes, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if len(b) <= limit:
        return b
    # Trim preferentially at boundaries of constructed parts by cutting at limit
    return b[:limit]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among several strategies to diversify inputs across calls
    choice = r.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        # Single printable label (good for sshbuf_new_label minimal case)
        out = _make_label(r)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Pure arbitrary blob up to 1024 (good for sshbuf_from backing)
        out = _make_arbitrary_payload(r, 1024)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Single SSH wire string with arbitrary payload (<=512)
        out = _ssh_wire_string(_make_arbitrary_payload(r, 512))
    elif choice == 3:
        # Single SSH wire string with cstring payload (<=512 but no NULs)
        out = _ssh_wire_string(_make_cstring_payload(r, 512))
    elif choice == 4:
        # Repeated pattern blob for formatting and put/putf paths
        out = _make_repeated_pattern(r, 768)
    else:
        # Mixed blob containing multiple useful segments
        out = _make_mixed_blob(r)

    return _ensure_size_limit(out, 4096)

import random
import secrets
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: C string (no NULs)
# Target usage: FUZZ_PARAM_STR feeding many APIs that expect
# - printable C strings (no embedded NULs) with diverse, interesting values
# - comma-separated name-lists for algorithms/ciphers
# - SSH algorithm/key/cipher names and variants
# - Reasonable sizes (many stubs cap to 512 or 1024)
#
# Strategy:
# - Encode a corpus of interesting strings that are valid C strings (no NULs)
# - Include known-good SSH names (KEX, hostkey algs, ciphers, MACs, compress)
# - Include edge cases: empty, single char, very long, repeated patterns, mixed case,
#   whitespace variants, comma-separated lists, duplicates, with/without spaces
# - Pack them as a length-prefixed series so the fuzzer framework can split them
#   into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions deterministically from one buffer.
#
# Buffer format (simple, self-describing, <= 4096 bytes):
#   [u16 count][ entries... ] where each entry is [u16 len][bytes]
#   All strings exclude NUL and are UTF-8 safe ASCII here.
#
# This enables the harness to take sequential substrings for each FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# If the harness directly uses the whole buffer for a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR,
# we still provide a diverse, comma-rich string first in the list.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_ENTRY = 1024

# Known-good pools
KEX_NAMES = [
    "diffie-hellman-group14-sha1",
    "diffie-hellman-group14-sha256",
    "diffie-hellman-group16-sha512",
    "diffie-hellman-group18-sha512",
    "diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256",
    "ecdh-sha2-nistp256",
    "ecdh-sha2-nistp384",
    "ecdh-sha2-nistp521",
    "curve25519-sha256",
    "curve25519-sha256@libssh.org",
    "sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com",
    "mlkem768x25519-sha256@openssh.com",
]

HOSTKEY_NAMES = [
    "ssh-ed25519",
    "ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com",
    "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256",
    "ecdsa-sha2-nistp384",
    "ecdsa-sha2-nistp521",
    "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com",
    "rsa-sha2-256",
    "rsa-sha2-512",
    "ssh-rsa",  # legacy
    "ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com",
]

CIPHERS = [
    "chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com",
    "aes128-ctr",
    "aes192-ctr",
    "aes256-ctr",
    "aes128-gcm@openssh.com",
    "aes256-gcm@openssh.com",
]

MACS = [
    "hmac-sha2-256",
    "hmac-sha2-512",
    "umac-64-etm@openssh.com",
    "umac-128-etm@openssh.com",
    "hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com",
    "hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com",
]

COMPRESS = [
    "none",
    "zlib@openssh.com",
    "zlib",
]

RSA_HASH_NAMES = [
    "rsa-sha2-256",
    "rsa-sha2-512",
    "ssh-rsa",  # maps to SHA1 in legacy paths
]

ECDSA_CURVES = [
    "nistp256",
    "nistp384",
    "nistp521",
]

KEY_SHORTNAMES = [
    "rsa",
    "ecdsa",
    "ed25519",
]

# Helper to ensure no NULs
def sanitize(s: str) -> str:
    # Replace any accidental NULs (shouldn't occur as we avoid them)
    return s.replace("\x00", "A")

# Build comma-separated lists with optional spaces
def name_list(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], allow_spaces: bool = True) -> str:
    k = rng.randint(1, min(6, len(items)))
    picks = rng.sample(items, k)
    if allow_spaces and rng.random() < 0.5:
        return ", ".join(picks)
    else:
        return ",".join(picks)

def random_word(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_@./+"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def big_string(rng: random.Random, target: int) -> str:
    # Build a long but valid cstring rich in commas and known tokens
    parts: List[str] = []
    pools = [KEX_NAMES, HOSTKEY_NAMES, CIPHERS, MACS, COMPRESS]
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) + max(0, len(parts) - 1) < target:
        pool = rng.choice(pools)
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice(pool))
        else:
            parts.append(random_word(rng, 3, 10))
    s = ",".join(parts)
    if len(s) > target:
        s = s[:target]
    return s

def pack_entries(entries: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # u16 count then u16 length per entry
    out = bytearray()
    out += len(entries).to_bytes(2, 'big')
    for e in entries:
        out += len(e).to_bytes(2, 'big')
        out += e
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) A rich primary string suitable for many consumers (<= 512)
    primary_len = rng.randint(64, 512)
    primary = big_string(rng, primary_len)
    entries.append(sanitize(primary).encode('utf-8'))

    # 2) Valid KEX name lists
    entries.append(sanitize(name_list(rng, KEX_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(KEX_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 3) Hostkey alg names and lists
    entries.append(sanitize(name_list(rng, HOSTKEY_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(HOSTKEY_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 4) Cipher lists and single names (for cipher_by_name, ciphers_valid)
    entries.append(sanitize(name_list(rng, CIPHERS)).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(CIPHERS)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 5) MAC lists
    entries.append(sanitize(name_list(rng, MACS)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 6) Compression lists
    entries.append(sanitize(name_list(rng, COMPRESS)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 7) RSA hash/keyname mapping inputs
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(RSA_HASH_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 8) Curve names and ecdsa mapping
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(ECDSA_CURVES)).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize("ecdsa-sha2-" + rng.choice(ECDSA_CURVES)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 9) Key type names and shortnames
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(HOSTKEY_NAMES)).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize(rng.choice(KEY_SHORTNAMES)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 10) Comma-separated mixes for kex_names_cat/has_any_alg
    mix_a = name_list(rng, KEX_NAMES + HOSTKEY_NAMES + CIPHERS + MACS + COMPRESS)
    mix_b = name_list(rng, KEX_NAMES + HOSTKEY_NAMES + CIPHERS + MACS + COMPRESS)
    entries.append(sanitize(mix_a).encode('utf-8'))
    entries.append(sanitize(mix_b).encode('utf-8'))

    # 11) Strings for comments/passphrases/providers/apps (arbitrary but valid)
    for _ in range(6):
        w = random_word(rng, 0, 32)  # allow empty too
        entries.append(sanitize(w).encode('utf-8'))

    # 12) Longer message payload for signing/verifying (<= 1024)
    long_msg = big_string(rng, rng.randint(128, 1024))
    entries.append(sanitize(long_msg).encode('utf-8'))

    # 13) Signature-like blobs (still plain text, valid cstring)
    sig_like = "+".join(random_word(rng, 8, 16) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)))
    entries.append(sanitize(sig_like).encode('utf-8'))

    # 14) Edge cases
    entries.append(b"")  # empty string
    entries.append(b"a")  # single char
    entries.append(b" ")  # space
    entries.append(b",")  # comma
    entries.append(b"none")

    # 15) Very long but <= MAX_ENTRY
    very_long = big_string(rng, min(MAX_ENTRY, 800))
    entries.append(sanitize(very_long).encode('utf-8'))

    # 16) Name-lists with spaces around commas
    spaced = ", ".join([rng.choice(KEX_NAMES), rng.choice(HOSTKEY_NAMES), rng.choice(CIPHERS)])
    entries.append(sanitize(spaced).encode('utf-8'))

    # Trim to total size budget by removing tail entries if necessary
    packed = pack_entries(entries)
    while len(packed) > MAX_TOTAL and entries:
        entries.pop()  # drop least important
        packed = pack_entries(entries)

    return packed

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid raw byte buffers for a variety of OpenSSH sshbuf/
# sshpkt consumers present in the fuzzer stubs. The goal is to create inputs that
# are likely to be accepted and exercise different code paths while remaining valid.
#
# Strategy:
# - Provide a mix of payloads framed as SSH packets (binary packet length + type + payload)
#   to satisfy ssh_packet_process_incoming() and subsequent sshpkt_get*() calls.
# - Provide standalone SSH strings (len32 + bytes) to satisfy sshpkt_get_string* paths.
# - Provide bignum2-encoded integers for sshbuf_(put|get)_bignum2_bytes*.
# - Include random blobs of various sizes for dump/read/compare/poke and signature enc/dec.
# - Include plausible signature and key-like frames for sshkey_* signature helpers.
# - Provide sufficiently long buffers for cipher_get_length() and cipher_crypt() use.
# - Return a single buffer per call; fuzzer runtime will distribute to FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
#
# Buffer size cap: <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Helpers to build SSH wire types

def u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', n & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def ssh_string(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return u32(len(b)) + b


def ssh_name_list(names: List[str]) -> bytes:
    s = ','.join(names).encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return ssh_string(s)


def make_packet(payload: bytes, pkt_type: int = None) -> bytes:
    # SSH binary packet: [packet_length][padding_length][payload(type+data)][random_padding]
    # For simplicity use minimalistic SSH-like structure; many paths only need data passed to engine.
    # We will mimic post-decryption cleartext framing used by sshpkt_* (len includes payload+padlen+1).
    if pkt_type is None:
        pkt_type = random.randint(1, 255)
    pl = bytes([pkt_type]) + payload
    # padding_length must make total_length % 8 == 0 and be at least 4
    # total_length = 1(padlen) + len(pl) + padlen
    # Choose padlen between 4..16 and adjust to 8-byte multiple
    padlen = random.randint(4, 16)
    total_no_len = 1 + len(pl) + padlen
    rem = total_no_len % 8
    if rem != 0:
        need = (8 - rem)
        padlen += need
        total_no_len += need
    padding = os.urandom(padlen)
    pkt = u32(total_no_len) + bytes([padlen]) + pl + padding
    return pkt

# Bignum2 encoding per OpenSSH: 4-byte length N, then N bytes big-endian magnitude,
# with an extra leading 0x00 if high bit of first byte would indicate negative when interpreted as signed.

def bignum2_from_bytes(mag: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(mag) == 0:
        mag = b"\x00"
    # Strip leading zeros in magnitude as typical, but keep one if all zero
    i = 0
    while i + 1 < len(mag) and mag[i] == 0:
        i += 1
    mag = mag[i:]
    if mag[0] & 0x80:
        mag = b"\x00" + mag
    return u32(len(mag)) + mag

# Make a plausible signature blob: string alg; string sigraw

def make_sig_blob(alg: str, sigraw: bytes) -> bytes:
    return ssh_string(alg.encode('ascii', 'ignore')) + ssh_string(sigraw)

# Generate a few different valid payload families and concatenate them with separators.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    random.seed(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) A small SSH packet carrying an SSH string so sshpkt_get_string* can succeed
    s1 = b"hello, world!" * rnd.randint(1, 4)
    pkt1 = make_packet(ssh_string(s1), pkt_type=rnd.randint(20, 60))
    parts.append(pkt1)

    # 2) Another packet with several fields: u8, u32, string
    field_u8 = bytes([rnd.randrange(0, 256)])
    field_u32 = u32(rnd.getrandbits(32))
    field_str = ssh_string(os.urandom(rnd.randint(1, 64)))
    payload2 = field_u8 + field_u32 + field_str
    pkt2 = make_packet(payload2, pkt_type=rnd.randint(1, 255))
    parts.append(pkt2)

    # 3) A bare SSH string blob for sshpkt_get_string_from stream cases
    bare_str = ssh_string(os.urandom(rnd.randint(8, 128)))
    parts.append(bare_str)

    # 4) Bignum2-encoded integers: small, medium, with/without high bit set
    bn_small = bignum2_from_bytes((rnd.randrange(1, 255)).to_bytes(1, 'big'))
    bn_medium_mag = os.urandom(rnd.randint(2, 64))
    # force high bit path sometimes
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        bn_medium_mag = bytes([bn_medium_mag[0] | 0x80]) + bn_medium_mag[1:]
    bn_medium = bignum2_from_bytes(bn_medium_mag)
    parts.append(bn_small)
    parts.append(bn_medium)

    # 5) Data blocks for sshbuf_dump_data / read/write scenarios
    dump_block = os.urandom(rnd.randint(16, 256))
    parts.append(dump_block)

    # 6) Signature blobs for sshkey_check_sigtype/get_sigtype
    # Ed25519-like
    sig_ed25519_raw = os.urandom(64)
    sig_ed = make_sig_blob('ssh-ed25519', sig_ed25519_raw)
    parts.append(sig_ed)
    # RSA-SHA256-like
    sig_rsa_raw = os.urandom(rnd.randint(48, 128))
    sig_rsa = make_sig_blob('rsa-sha2-256', sig_rsa_raw)
    parts.append(sig_rsa)

    # 7) Cipher-oriented random buffers of certain lengths for get_length/crypt
    cipher_buf = os.urandom(rnd.randint(8, 96))
    parts.append(cipher_buf)

    # 8) Name-list proposals useful for KEX-related code paths (as generic data)
    kex_names = ['curve25519-sha256', 'diffie-hellman-group14-sha1', 'sntrup761x25519-sha512']
    mac_names = ['hmac-sha2-256', 'hmac-sha2-512', 'umac-64-etm@openssh.com']
    enc_names = ['chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com', 'aes128-ctr', 'aes256-gcm@openssh.com']
    nl_blob = ssh_name_list(rnd.sample(kex_names, rnd.randint(1, len(kex_names)))) \
        + ssh_name_list(rnd.sample(enc_names, rnd.randint(1, len(enc_names)))) \
        + ssh_name_list(rnd.sample(mac_names, rnd.randint(1, len(mac_names))))
    parts.append(nl_blob)

    # 9) Another packet focusing on small read sizes for sshpkt_get_u8/u32/u64
    payload3 = bytes([rnd.randrange(0, 256)]) + u32(rnd.getrandbits(32)) + struct.pack('>Q', rnd.getrandbits(64))
    pkt3 = make_packet(payload3, pkt_type=rnd.randint(1, 255))
    parts.append(pkt3)

    # 10) Additional raw blob for sshbuf_find/sshbuf_cmp usage
    alpha = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    frag = bytearray()
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(32, 128)):
        frag.append(alpha[rnd.randrange(0, len(alpha))])
    parts.append(bytes(frag))

    # Concatenate with small random separators to avoid accidental merges harming parsers
    out = bytearray()
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        if len(out) + len(p) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += p
        # add small separator sometimes
        if i + 1 < len(parts) and rnd.random() < 0.5:
            sep = os.urandom(rnd.randint(1, 8))
            if len(out) + len(sep) <= MAX_TOTAL:
                out += sep

    # Ensure non-empty and capped
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(os.urandom(32))
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return bytes(out)
